question: If a NEW plaque is used to call attention to a new sign, how long should it remain, and may strobe lights be used to enhance sign conspicuity?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A NEW plaque used to call attention to a new sign should remain in place for a period determined by engineering judgment, but not more than 12 months, and should be removed no later than 12 months after installation. Strobe lights are prohibited as a means of enhancing sign conspicuity. Standards (mandatory): - "Strobe lights shall not be used to enhance the conspicuity of highway signs." Guidance (recommended): - If a NEW plaque is used, it should remain in place for a period of time determined by engineering judgment, but not more than 12 months. - The NEW plaque should be removed no later than 12 months after it was installed. Options (permitted): - A NEW plaque may be added above a new standard regulatory or warning sign, for a period of time in accordance with the guidance above, to call attention to the new sign, based on engineering judgment as one of several permitted methods of enhancing sign conspicuity. - A NEW (W16-15P) plaque may be mounted above a regulatory sign when a new regulation takes effect to alert road users to the new traffic regulation, and may also be mounted above an advance warning sign (such as a Signal Ahead sign for a newly-installed traffic control signal) to warn of a new traffic condition. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Guidance §3 (p.49) - Section 2C.60 Guidance §2 (p.197) - Section 2A.11 Standard §4 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 2C.60 Option §1 (p.197)
gold_answer: The NEW plaque should remain only for a period determined by engineering judgment and no more than 12 months. Strobe lights may not be used to enhance highway-sign conspicuity.
